001.summary: The first game ever played with the deck (no result logged; a pod of three at home). A Sol Ring opening made it fast, and Brallin and Shabraz got big off discards and draws. A late wheel (the note's 'Edge of Eons', which on this list reads as Echo of Eons) 'almost killed Stuart through commander damage'. After that it went grindy: Brallin was removed twice and picked up commander tax, the deck drew no ramp past the opening, and it had no creature or enchantment removal against Steven's counters. Played on v7 (decklist_sha256 ce0ceaa6…, 2026-10-06), not the current v2.0.0. Several cards the note names have since left the 99: Mana Geyser (gone by v1.3.0), and Swiftfoot Boots, Echo of Eons and the 'wheel on a stick' (Magus of the Wheel on that list) were cut at v2.0.0. Read those as notes about the list that was played, not errors.

opponents.evidence: Steven had a bunch of freaking counters that he was playing

cards.why: 'it started off pretty fast, but that's because I had Sol Ring in my opening hand'
'Lightning Greaves ... were really good and and protected them' (the note says the same of the Swiftfoot Boots then in the list)
'Brawn got taken out a couple times' and 'he got removed a couple times and then the tax came on'
a wheel 'made Shabraz really big' and 'almost killed Stuart through commander damage'
'I never pulled Jessica's Will or Mana Geyser' while the deck felt 'a little light on the ramp'
never drawn, named alongside Jeska's Will as the ramp the pilot was counting on. It has since left the 99

decisions.spot: which commander to deploy first, and whether to hold the second (and the wheels) until hand and board suit the pair: 'bring one out ... get that thing big and then like bring the second one out later and then start doing the wheels'
firing a wheel that discards 'some really useful things because I just needed to do the wheel'

takeaways: The two commanders cost nine mana as a pair ('basically equivalent to the Ur-Dragon'), and one removal stacks tax on top. Ramp past the opening hand felt light.
Protection (Lightning Greaves and the Boots then in the list) worked, but Brallin was still removed twice.
The deck had no creature or enchantment removal when the board needed pruning, and too little interaction against a counterspell seat, so the late game went grindy.
Piloting plan: one commander first, grow it, add the second later, and fire the wheels when both are on the board with protection up.
The pilot wants wheels that do a second job (a counter plus a wheel, removal plus a wheel) so that each slot covers two needs.
Wheels split the table ('people either loved it or hated it'), and they can cost the pilot his own good cards.

open_questions.question: On the current list, how often are both commanders (four plus five mana) on the battlefield by turns six to eight, and how often with one tax added after a removal?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot reads the pair as a nine-drop and felt ramp-light. Every wheel's payoff assumes both commanders are out

open_questions.question: Does the deck carry enough creature and enchantment removal, plus interaction against counterspells, to prune a board and get a wheel through a counterspell seat?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note blames the grindy late game on 'I didn't have enough interaction or removal'

open_questions.question: Which wheel effects in the corpus also counter a spell or remove permanents, the 'align on both axes' cards the pilot asked for?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot named this as what 'would be money', and he asked for the research agent to queue explorations

open_questions.question: Is 'one commander first, the second later, wheels only with both out' the right piloting plan for this pair?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the note proposes it as 'a piloting strategy', and game 002 says the same about when wheels should land

002.summary: A loss in a four-player pod at Oliver's, played on v8 (decklist_sha256 fda57c5a…, the v1.3.0 list), not the current v2.0.0. The pilot mulliganed and doubted the hand he kept, which had one playable creature and a bunch of wheels. Shabraz's wheels 'went pretty well', but his main finding is that the deck runs too many wheels. Wheels should be few, held as finishers for when both commanders are already out, partly because making the table discard over and over is politically costly. The v2.0.0 voltron merge has since cut several wheels from that list (Echo of Eons, Magus of the Wheel and Time Reversal among them). This annotation records what the pilot said; it does not judge whether that merge settles his point.

opponents.evidence: Oliver is making people discard creatures on the board and all this other stuff

decisions.spot: keep or mulligan a hand with 'only one playable creature in it and a bunch of wheels'
when to fire a wheel: early as card flow, or held until 'Shabraz and Brallin are already out, they're kind of big' as a finisher

takeaways: Too many wheels: 'I think there's too many wheels', and the kept hand had one creature and several wheels.
Wheels are finishers. They should land when both commanders are on the table and already big, then chain into a second wheel, with red open for trample.
Repeated wheels cost goodwill at the table ('Making people discard their hand is not something people enjoy'), which is one more reason to make them 'few and far between'.
Discount goldfish figures on this deck: they leave out removal and opponent interaction, and that 'just moves the deck in the wrong direction'.

open_questions.question: On the v2.0.0 list, how often does an opening seven hold at most one creature alongside two or more wheels, and how did that rate move from v1.3.0?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot's 'too many wheels' finding came from exactly that keep. A paired before-and-after rate would show whether the voltron merge addressed it

open_questions.question: With both commanders out and grown, does a wheel followed by a second wheel, then a flying, trampling commander attack ('into another one ... flying trample big commander shark coming at you'), kill a seat through commander damage?
open_questions.why_it_matters: this is the finisher sequence the pilot wants wheels saved for. Only the single-Windfall base line is proved (stack 001), and stack 005 shows one Windfall is not a kill from 40

open_questions.question: Is the deck's wheel count right for a list where wheels are finishers rather than card flow?
open_questions.why_it_matters: the pilot proposed recalibrating the deck around that role, and game 001 also asked for wheels held until both commanders are out
